rationale.conceptual: The method involves non-trivial solid-state physics: decomposition of specific heat into electronic, lattice (Debye+Einstein), and dilatation components; fitting an Einstein temperature; scaling via corresponding states; and bounding magnetic contributions under assumptions. It requires careful translation of established physical models into code, but is not a novel custom algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline comprises ~6 sequential stages (dilatation correction, acoustic contribution extraction, scaling, integration, bounding) with dependencies between them. It also requires fetching external numerical data (UN Cp from a 1966 paper), which adds engineering effort. However, standard Python libraries suffice, no complex tooling.
